lines.say: Chapter one. One tiny drop.
Holmes founded Theranos in two thousand three, and served as its chief executive until two thousand eighteen, according to the federal appeals court.
lines.show: Holmes founded Theranos in 2003, and served as its chief executive until 2018, according to the federal appeals court.

scene.src: U.S. Court of Appeals, 9th Cir., No. 22-10312 (amended Dec 22, 2025)

lines.say: The court opened its opinion with the vision she sold. One tiny drop changes everything.

scene.doc: THE VISION · AS QUOTED BY THE COURT

lines.say: Theranos claimed, the court wrote, that it could run fast, accurate and affordable tests with just a drop of blood drawn from the prick of a finger.

scene.title: “just a drop of blood”
scene.src: U.S. Court of Appeals, 9th Cir., No. 22-10312 (amended Dec 22, 2025)

lines.say: In two thousand ten, Theranos partnered with Walgreens. In the fall of two thousand thirteen, it launched its testing services in Walgreens stores, then raised new money from investors.
lines.show: In 2010, Theranos partnered with Walgreens. In the fall of 2013, it launched its testing services in Walgreens stores, then raised new money from investors.

scene.src: U.S. Court of Appeals, 9th Cir., No. 22-10312 (amended Dec 22, 2025)

lines.say: By the end of two thousand fourteen, prosecutors said, Holmes's own shares in Theranos were valued at more than four billion dollars.
lines.show: By the end of 2014, prosecutors said, Holmes's own shares in Theranos were valued at more than $4 billion.

scene.label: the value of Holmes's own|Theranos shares

lines.say: She was on the covers of Fortune and Forbes. Time named her one of the hundred most influential people in the world.
lines.show: She was on the covers of Fortune and Forbes. Time named her one of the 100 most influential people in the world.

lines.say: Chapter two. The pitch.

Prosecutors laid out what Holmes told investors. One Theranos device could run any blood test a conventional lab could, from a fingerstick. Major drug companies had validated it. The military was using it. And the business was profitable.

In truth, the government said, the Theranos device could never complete more than twelve types of blood tests. To fill out its menu, the company quietly used modified and unmodified machines made by other companies.
lines.show: In truth, the government said, the Theranos device could never complete more than 12 types of blood tests. To fill out its menu, the company quietly used modified and unmodified machines made by other companies.

scene.title: “never complete more than 12 types of blood tests”

lines.say: Theranos had zero revenue in two thousand twelve and two thousand thirteen. Yet investors were given projections of one hundred forty million dollars in revenue for two thousand fourteen, and nearly one billion for two thousand fifteen.
lines.show: Theranos had zero revenue in 2012 and 2013. Yet investors were given projections of $140 million in revenue for 2014, and nearly $1 billion for 2015.

lines.say: Behind the projections, the appeals court noted, Balwani told Holmes in November two thousand thirteen that Theranos was down to fifteen million dollars in cash, and spending up to two million dollars a week. In two thousand fifteen, it reported less than two million dollars in total income to the IRS.
lines.show: Behind the projections, the appeals court noted, Balwani told Holmes in November 2013 that Theranos was down to $15 million in cash, and spending up to $2 million a week. In 2015, it reported less than $2 million in total income to the IRS.

lines: Spending up to|$2 million a week.
scene.src: U.S. Court of Appeals, 9th Cir., No. 22-10312 (amended Dec 22, 2025)

lines.say: Investors were also told the device was being used on medevac helicopters and on the battlefield. According to the government, the Defense Department never used it to treat patients.

scene.title: “never used Theranos' device to clinically treat patients”

lines.say: At technology demonstrations, the court wrote, VIP guests were led to believe the device was running a sample of their blood. In reality, it was running a null protocol, while some samples were secretly run on other companies' machines.

scene.q: In reality, the device was running a “null protocol” while some of the VIP samples were surreptitiously run on third-party devices.

lines.say: Then there were the reports. In April two thousand ten, prosecutors said, Holmes emailed Walgreens executives reports with favorable conclusions about Theranos, bearing the logos of Pfizer, GlaxoSmithKline and Schering-Plough.
lines.show: Then there were the reports. In April 2010, prosecutors said, Holmes emailed Walgreens executives reports with favorable conclusions about Theranos, bearing the logos of Pfizer, GlaxoSmithKline and Schering-Plough.

lines.say: At trial, Holmes admitted that she personally put those logos on the reports. Witnesses from the drug companies testified that they had not validated the technology, and had not authorized the use of their logos.

lines.say: Chapter three. The unraveling.
Inside the company, prosecutors said, scientists warned Holmes in two thousand thirteen that the device could not reliably test patient samples. Some resigned shortly before the Walgreens launch.
lines.show: Inside the company, prosecutors said, scientists warned Holmes in 2013 that the device could not reliably test patient samples. Some resigned shortly before the Walgreens launch.

lines.say: One scientist testified about Holmes's response: she has a promise to deliver to the customer.

scene.q: she has a promise to deliver to the customer, she doesn't have much of a choice but to go ahead with the launch.
scene.cite: As quoted in the gov't sentencing memorandum, Nov 11, 2022

lines.say: In September two thousand fifteen, Balwani texted Holmes: Our validation reports are terrible. Her reply: Praying.
lines.show: In September 2015, Balwani texted Holmes: "Our validation reports are terrible." Her reply: "Praying."

lines.say: In late two thousand fifteen, news reporting revealed internal struggles inside the Theranos laboratory.
lines.show: In late 2015, news reporting revealed internal struggles inside the Theranos laboratory.

scene.src: U.S. Court of Appeals, 9th Cir., No. 22-10312 (amended Dec 22, 2025)

lines.say: According to prosecutors, when Holmes learned that a Wall Street Journal reporter was working on the story, she hired the lawyer David Boies to try to get him to drop it. Then she appealed to the newspaper's owner, who was also a significant Theranos investor.
Asked on television about it, Holmes said that every test that we offer in our laboratory can run on our proprietary devices. Prosecutors said that was false.

scene.q: every test that we offer in our laboratory can run on our proprietary devices.
scene.cite: As quoted in the gov't sentencing memorandum, Nov 11, 2022

lines.say: Federal regulators inspected the lab. Faced with their findings, Theranos itself admitted a global and long-term failure of the quality control program for its device.
Theranos voided every patient test result ever run on that device in its clinical lab.

March fourteenth, two thousand eighteen. The Securities and Exchange Commission charged Theranos, Holmes and Balwani with what it called a massive fraud that raised more than seven hundred million dollars from investors.
lines.show: March 14, 2018. The Securities and Exchange Commission charged Theranos, Holmes and Balwani with what it called a "massive fraud" that raised more than $700 million from investors.

scene.label: raised from investors,|according to the SEC

lines.say: Holmes settled. She agreed to a five hundred thousand dollar penalty, a ten-year bar from serving as an officer or director of a public company, and to give up voting control of Theranos.
lines.show: Holmes settled. She agreed to a $500,000 penalty, a ten-year bar from serving as an officer or director of a public company, and to give up voting control of Theranos.

items: Barred as public-company officer or director

lines.say: Investors are entitled to nothing less than complete truth and candor, said the SEC's enforcement co-director.

scene.q: Investors are entitled to nothing less than complete truth and candor from companies and their executives

lines.say: Three months later, on June fourteenth, a federal grand jury in California indicted Holmes and Balwani for wire fraud.
lines.show: Three months later, on June 14, a federal grand jury in California indicted Holmes and Balwani for wire fraud.

scene.title: The United States of America v. Holmes & Balwani

lines.say: Chapter four. The trial.
The final indictment charged two conspiracies, one against investors and one against patients, and ten counts of wire fraud. The court tried Holmes and Balwani separately.

scene.title: Third Superseding Indictment
scene.src: Third Superseding Indictment, Dkt. 469, N.D. Cal., Jul 28, 2020 · Gov't sentencing memorandum, Dkt. 1643, Nov 11, 2022

lines.say: Holmes's trial began on August thirty-first, two thousand twenty-one. It lasted four months. Thirty-two witnesses testified, and more than nine hundred exhibits were admitted.
lines.show: Holmes's trial began on August 31, 2021. It lasted four months. 32 witnesses testified, and more than 900 exhibits were admitted.

lines.say: At trial, prosecutors said, she blamed her chief operating officer, her board, her scientists, her business partners, her investors, the media. Everyone, that is, but herself.

scene.q: At trial, she blamed her COO (and longtime boyfriend), her board, her scientists, her business partners, her investors, her marketing firm, her attorneys, the media—everyone, that is, but herself.

lines.say: The verdict: guilty of conspiracy to defraud investors, and of three counts of wire fraud. The wires behind those counts: thirty-eight million dollars in February two thousand fourteen, and nearly one hundred million and six million dollars on October thirty-first, two thousand fourteen.
lines.show: The verdict: guilty of conspiracy to defraud investors, and of three counts of wire fraud. The wires behind those counts: $38 million in February 2014, and nearly $100 million and $6 million on October 31, 2014.

scene.src: Third Superseding Indictment, Dkt. 469, N.D. Cal., Jul 28, 2020

lines.say: Not guilty on four counts: the conspiracy against patients, and three related wire fraud counts. The court declared a mistrial on the three counts where the jury deadlocked. Prosecutors later dismissed them.

lines.say: Chapter five. The sentence.

November eighteenth, two thousand twenty-two. Prosecutors asked for fifteen years. The probation office recommended nine. Her lawyers argued for eighteen months or less, and suggested home confinement.
lines.show: November 18, 2022. Prosecutors asked for 15 years. The probation office recommended nine. Her lawyers argued for 18 months or less, and suggested home confinement.

lines.say: The probation office had put investor losses at more than seven hundred thirty million dollars. The judge found that too high. Theranos stock, he reasoned, was not practically worthless, and kept some value apart from the fraud.
